description_full: Columbia Financial, Inc. operates as a bank holding company for Columbia Bank that provides banking and other financial services to businesses and consumers in the United States. The company offers deposit products, including non-interest and interest-bearing demand accounts, savings and club deposits, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit. It also provides commercial loans, including multifamily and commercial real estate, commercial business, and construction loans; residential loans, such as one-to-four family residential real estate and one-to-four family residential loans; consumer loans, which includes home equity loans and advances, as well as automobile, personal, unsecured, and overdraft lines of credit; and securities activities. In addition, the company offers title insurance products; wealth management services; and cash management services comprising remote deposit, lockbox service, sweep accounts, and escrow services. Columbia Financial, Inc. was founded in 1926 and is based in Fair Lawn, New Jersey.

financial_summary: Columbia Financial, Inc. is a mid-cap financial services business with a $3.0B market cap on $259M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

The business throws off $59M in free cash flow — roughly 23 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.32× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 56.1× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss.

Shareholder yield of 2.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 29% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
